What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(-4,-2)$ and passes through the point $(8,-6).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-4,-2),$ we substitute $h=-4$ and $k=-2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(8,-6),$ so we can substitute $x=8$ and $y=-6$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ (-6+2)^{2} & =4p(8+4) \\ 16 & =48p \\ p & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{3})(x+4) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =\frac{4}{3}(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{1}{3}$ is positive.
